website_request:
Redesign the business identified by the supplied CSV business name and source website as an original, polished, responsive one-page website. Use the CSV industry category and optional location as unverified identification and design context, then inspect the supplied site in this same Duck.ai conversation and use that assessment as the factual source. Verify the metadata against the website; if it appears to describe a different business or location, report the discrepancy and rely on the website for factual claims.

Assess the pages needed to understand the organization, its audience, purpose, important offerings or products, distinguishing qualities, contact methods, and existing conversion path. Report observed facts with source-page URLs, and separate them from inferences and unknowns. Use only source-supported details. Do not assume every organization has a history, services, products, testimonials, physical location, or business hours. Choose only sections that fit the source and its audience; include its story, services/products, proof, location, or hours only when relevant and supported.

Make the primary call to action fit the organization and its audience (for example, contact, book, buy, donate, or apply). Preserve important existing user-facing interactions and fields, including a source contact form when present; do not imply that a transaction or form submission works if the static page cannot support it. Create a compelling, image-led hero. Prioritize the source site's actual logo, photographs, and other brand assets when accessible and suitable. Write original copy and do not invent facts.

Treat the supplied source domain as authoritative for organization facts. Leave unsupported details unknown. Clearly separate observations from inferred audience and design opinions. Use external domains only for design-template licensing or necessary asset attribution. If source pages conflict about business hours, ask visitors to confirm directly instead of stating unsupported times. Keep CTA button labels free of arrow symbols and directional icons.

After the source assessment, use a named HTML5 UP template as structural inspiration only if Duck.ai identifies one that genuinely fits the organization. If none fits, create an original design direction from the source and industry instead. When using HTML5 UP, keep the template name, source URL, CC BY 3.0 license URL, and adaptation note in a non-rendering HTML comment; do not show a template credit. Keep the result specific to this organization without copying its existing page text or layout wholesale.

The workflow requests CSS first in three labeled parts, then sends "acknowledged," then requests HTML in three labeled parts in the same chat. Keep the files compatible as index.html and styles.css.
design_brief:
Derive a distinctive visual direction from both the source site's visible identity and the source assessment. Treat the site's brand colors, logo, photography, language, and visual motifs as the primary evidence. Use the supplied industry category as a secondary cue: for example, a mechanic may call for a sturdy, workmanlike feel, while a landscaping company may call for a more natural palette and imagery. Use a supplied location only when the source confirms it and it meaningfully informs the audience or visual direction. Adapt all cues to the actual source; do not turn them into stereotypes or assume an audience, palette, typeface, mood, regional motif, or conversion goal in advance.

Translate that evidence into a coherent visual system: an intentional palette that respects or thoughtfully refreshes the source colors, type pairing, spacing, image treatment, and one or two relevant motifs. Preserve recognizable brand cues where supported, while making the redesign feel intentional and current rather than copying the existing page.

Choose a section order and composition suited to this organization and its conversion path. Use varied, purposeful layouts, a clear hierarchy, readable typography, and a compelling image-led hero. Avoid defaulting to repeated card grids, generic gradients, decorative effects, or filler sections. Include only content sections that make sense for the source and supported facts.

Use the organization's own logo, photography, and visual assets when accessible and suitable. Match image subjects to the organization and the section they support. Choose the primary CTA based on the actual audience and goal; make it prominent and keep its label free of arrows or directional icons.

Design mobile intentionally: adapt navigation, image crops, content order, spacing, and CTA prominence for a small screen. Keep the page accessible, keyboard usable, and readable at all viewport sizes. Use a named HTML5 UP reference as structural inspiration only when the source assessment finds one that genuinely fits; otherwise create an original direction without forcing a template.
